meta.title: Nevada Window Tint Law, Explained | BC Glass & Tint
meta.description: What NRS 484D.440 says: 35 percent light on front side windows with a 7 percent tolerance, nonreflective film, and the rules for the windshield and rear glass.

v3.lede: One hard number for your front side windows: the glass and film together must pass no less than 35 percent of light, with a 7 percent tolerance, and the film cannot be reflective. Every rule below comes straight from the statute, cited line by line.

blocks.heading: What NRS 484D.440 says.
blocks.lede: Five provisions, each cited. Nothing on this page beyond these five is stated as law.

items.term: The combined light transmission through your front side glass and film cannot drop below 35 percent, with a 7 percent measurement tolerance.
items.detail: This is visible light transmission, or VLT, for the glass and film together, not the film by itself.

items.term: Film on the front side windows must be nonreflective.
items.detail: A mirrored or reflective finish on the front side windows is not allowed, regardless of how dark it is.

items.term: Film is not allowed on the windshield except a strip across the topmost portion, subject to a bottom-edge height requirement, and it cannot be red or amber.
items.detail: The exact height that strip can reach down to is set by the statute's own bottom-edge rule.

items.term: The rear window and back side windows may be tinted if the vehicle has outside mirrors on both sides that show at least 200 feet behind you.
items.detail: With that mirror setup in place, the statute does not set a separate darkness limit for the rear and back side windows.

items.term: On exemptions, the statute says only that the Director may provide for exemptions and exceptions by regulation.
items.detail: The statute does not spell out who qualifies or how.

blocks.note: Read the statute yourself: Nevada Revised Statutes 484D.440.

blocks.heading: What this means for you.
paragraphs: We install film that meets Nevada's front-window rule and can point you to the darkest shade the law still allows. We install ceramic film, so a legal front shade still cuts glare.

We do not know the specific criteria for a medical or any other exemption, and we will not guess at a number or a process we cannot verify. If you believe you qualify, contact the issuing authority directly.

items.question: Is 35 percent the same as 35 percent tint?
items.answer: Not exactly. The 35 percent figure in the law is VLT, the share of light that passes through the glass and film together. People shorten it to 35 percent tint, but the number describes how much light gets through, not a darkness rating for the film alone. Source: Nevada Revised Statutes 484D.440.

items.question: Can my back windows be darker?
items.answer: Yes, with one condition. Your rear window and back side windows can be tinted as long as your vehicle has outside mirrors on both sides that give you a view of at least 200 feet behind you. Source: Nevada Revised Statutes 484D.440.

items.question: Can you tint my windshield?
items.answer: Only the top strip. Nevada law does not allow film on the windshield except a strip across the very top, and how far down it can reach is set by a bottom-edge height rule in the statute. The strip cannot be red or amber. Source: Nevada Revised Statutes 484D.440.
